text:
maria: heads up — i'm seeing a weird auth gap after yesterday's key rotation. a token with only `embeddings:write` scope succeeded calling /v1/chat/respond twice in a row from the same client session.
kevin: whoa. repro reliably?
maria: not 100% reliable, but i can reproduce locally if i keep the same session-id and hammer it with 10 requests. after rotate it fails for a bit then allows chat calls for a handful of requests, then fails again.
elaine: sounds like a cache or sticky-session issue in the auth middleware — maybe scope info is cached per connection? does client use connection affinity to the same worker?
maria: yes, our test client sets X-Session-ID header. if i change it it fails immediately.
sam: can you paste logs (redact tokens) for one of the runs?
maria: sure, snippet below: 
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] auth: token=redacted scope=[embeddings:write] route=/v1/chat/respond decision=ALLOW (cache_age_ms=3)
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] runtime: routed to worker-7 (sticky=true)
[2026-03-18T14:02:31Z] chat: request accepted by model-mux
[2026-03-18T14:02:32Z] audit: event=api_call token_id=abc123 route=/v1/chat/respond scope_used=embeddings:write
[2026-03-18T14:02:33Z] auth: token=redacted route=/v1/chat/respond decision=DENY (cache_age_ms=120000)
```
kevin: the audit line showing scope_used=embeddings:write for a chat route is particularly concerning — that implies enforcement allowed a mismatched scope. is enforcement happening at the gateway or the worker?
elaine: we do a fast-path cache check in the gateway and also a worker-side verification for critical routes, but the worker check is async/soft-fail to avoid latency spikes — maybe the rotation created a window where the gateway trusted stale cache and worker hadn't loaded updated scope metadata.
maria: i hit a variation where KMS rotated the wrapping key and the token metadata store returned 500 for ~30s. during that window some requests used fallback cached metadata.
sam: so potential root causes: 1) cache TTL too long for per-route scope changes 2) sticky session affinity keeping requests on worker with stale auth context 3) soft-fail policy on worker allowing gap during upstream errors.
kevin: agree. propose short-term mitigation: reduce gateway auth cache TTL to 5s for scope lookups during rotation windows, and disable sticky affinity for auth-sensitive endpoints via config. also make worker verification hard-fail when scope mismatch for high-risk routes (chat/response).
elaine: we should also add audit log correlation: include scope_source and cache_age_ms in audit entries so we can tell whether the gateway or worker approved.
audit-bot: noted. creating incident ticket SEC-2026-142 and tagging oncall.
maria: i can put a quick repro script in infra-test that toggles X-Session-ID loop and hits both /v1/embeddings and /v1/chat to produce diff logs. will attach to ticket.
sam: long-term: rework auth metadata propagation to use versioned tokens or a cache-invalidation pubsub so workers immediately evict on rotation. also add KMS rotation choreography to block live auth decisions until metadata verified.
kevin: i'll draft the change: gateway TTL -> 5s, disable affinity flag for chat routes, worker verify change = hard-fail on scope mismatch. PR will include telemetry for count of cross-scope approvals.
elaine: can we also add a test that simulates KMS downtime during rotation and asserts no cross-scope approvals? put it in eng-ml/canary.
maria: yep i'll add the test and link after ticket is made.
sam: thanks — make sure to tag product/security for customer-facing impact statement, and coordinate a postmortem if we find any production exposures. :eyes:
kevin: filing PR draft now. ping once ticket has repro artifacts. :thumbsup:
